item.text: {"claim_count":14,"content_failure_reasons":["Claim 6 overstates the Mexican Bank Association's role: the extract says it sets the domestic payment system's rules and operational standards, not that it runs the system.","Claim 9's qualification recasts the digital identity document as merely announced, whereas the extract says the government created it in 2020; only the digital National Population Registry's future operability is qualified.","The map says macroeconomic and competition material is outside the extract, but page 127 contains directly relevant assertions about macroeconomic stability, weakened growth, fiscal-policy capacity, investment, business regulation, competition, informality, and corruption."],"content_usable":false,"material_omission":true,"material_omission_explanation":"Page 127 materially supplies evidence for the questions the map labels absent or requiring reopening: it states that Mexico's macroeconomic framework safeguarded stability, medium-term growth prospects weakened, fiscal policy's capacity to smooth cycles and support recessions could be enhanced, and reforms were needed in business regulation, competition, informality, and corruption. Omitting this material and asserting that 5B.3–5B.5 are outside the chunk distorts decisive chapter coverage. The map also omits the page 105 pandemic-era firm-digitalisation initiatives and their expressly uncertain effectiveness, but that secondary omission alone would not make the content unusable.","schema_version":"reader_content_audit_v1","source_id":"MAC-015","supported_claim_count":12,"unsupported_claim_count":2,"usable_locator_count":14}
